children.value: A BIOPAC MP160 with an ECG100C amplifier recorded the ECG during the whole session. This chapter describes how the ECG is aligned with the task, how R peaks are detected and corrected, the heart-rate measures per trial and per session, and the data quality.

Triggers and alignment with the task

children.label: Triggers and alignment with the task

children.value: The task sets the trigger line high for 100 ms at every event: experiment start, trial start, cue onset (
), placement onset, ISI onset, attack onset (
) and the end of the feedback screen (

). All events give the same pulse, so the pulses carry no event code. Trial start and cue onset are 102 ms apart, and their two pulses can merge into one pulse of about 200 ms; a pulse longer than 150 ms is split into two onsets.
The expected event times on the task clock come from the result files: trial start (

) plus the onsets of the cue, placement, ISI and outcome relative to it, in ms. The offset between the task clock and the ECG clock is the mode of all differences between pulse onsets and expected events. The ECG clock runs about 23 ppm fast relative to the task computer (about 80 ms per hour), so the offset is estimated in each quarter of the session as a starting value. Each expected event is then matched to the nearest pulse (within 50 ms, then within 15 ms), and ECG time = a + b × task time is fitted by least squares. The windows below use the matched pulse onsets (the fitted time where no pulse was matched).

The event logs store the computer time after each pulse. In 8 logs these time stamps jump by minutes relative to the pulse train, so the logs serve only as a check. For participant 11623, who has no result file, the EyeLink messages provide the expected events.

94 participants remain, 93 of them in the analysis sample (None 36, Partial 35, Full 22). HRV of the task segment is missing for 7 of them: 14704, 14776, 15313, 15577, 16381, 8500 and 9304 (valid time below 90 % or more than 5 % corrected beats). HRV is available for 347 of the 370 blocks.
Task time covered by valid intervals

Of 455,010 beats in the task, the correction changed 298 ectopic, 236 missed, 16 extra and 1,744 long or short beats; 5,825 detections with a template correlation below .50 were removed. 21 recordings were inverted. In 4 of them (11302, 12157, 14137, 15388) about half of the windows voted for inversion; their beat-template correlations are at least .97. Usable windows: cue 99.1 % of 16,859 trials; attack 99.3 % and feedback 99.2 % of the 15,199 trials with an attack.
